gaps.sentence: 'Someone has stolen my bike,' he cried. He cried that someone ___ his bike.
gaps.explanation: have stolen backshifts to had stolen after the past reporting verb 'cried'.

gaps.sentence: 'They were arguing all through dinner,' he said. He said they ___ arguing all through dinner.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: were arguing → had been arguing.

gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'I really must have that report by five,' the editor said. The editor ___ on having the report by five.
gaps.explanation: Insisting on a demand: insist on + -ing (or insist that + clause).

gaps.sentence: 'How long have you worked here?' she asked him. She asked him how long he ___ there.
gaps.explanation: have worked → had worked; 'here' becomes 'there' in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave the building immediately!' the firefighter ordered. The firefighter ordered us ___ the building immediately.
gaps.explanation: Orders are reported with order + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'When did the ancient city fall?' we asked the guide. We asked the guide when the ancient city ___.
gaps.explanation: did...fall → had fallen: the auxiliary 'did' disappears and the verb backshifts.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.
